acceptance_criteria.criterion: A .wp-timing CSS rule exists in mcp-server/gui/public/styles.css with at minimum margin-top and a color/font-size token consistent with other metadata card blocks
The wp-timing div in the WP detail view no longer renders as an unstyled inline block
PipelineSchema.duration_ms in mcp-server/src/schema/work-package.ts uses z.number().int().nonnegative().optional() instead of z.number().optional()
All 1481+ MCP server Vitest tests pass after both changes

summary: Added .wp-timing CSS rule to mcp-server/gui/public/styles.css (at end of file, after pipeline stage dark-theme overrides). The rule sets margin-top: 12px, font-size: 12px, and color: var(--color-text-muted) — consistent with .pipeline-meta and other metadata card blocks throughout the stylesheet.

Updated PipelineSchema.duration_ms in mcp-server/src/schema/work-package.ts from z.number().optional() to z.number().int().nonnegative().optional() to enforce that duration_ms is always a non-negative integer (milliseconds cannot be fractional or negative).
Full MCP server Vitest test suite: 1518 tests passed (50 test files). Well above the 1481+ threshold.

comments.note: mcp-server/gui/public/styles.css: .wp-timing currently has no display property — it inherits block from the div element which is correct. The rule is intentionally minimal: it brings the timing block in line with .pipeline-meta and .pipeline-comments visually. If the timing block ever needs layout changes (e.g. flex for icon+text), a single property addition suffices.

mcp-server/src/schema/work-package.ts PipelineSchema: the .int().nonnegative() chain is a strict improvement but has a subtle nuance — any existing data with a fractional duration_ms (e.g. 5000.5) would now fail zod parsing. In practice the MCP server always writes integer ms values, so this is safe. Worth noting for any data migration scenarios.
No further observations — both changes are minimal, targeted, and consistent with existing patterns.

summary: Reviewed mcp-server/gui/public/styles.css: .wp-timing rule at line 1691 sets margin-top:12px, font-size:12px, color:var(--color-text-muted). Verified --color-text-muted is defined in both light (#64748b) and dark (#94a3b8) CSS root blocks. The token values and font-size exactly match .pipeline-meta (lines 586-590), confirming visual consistency with the rest of the metadata card pattern.

Reviewed mcp-server/src/schema/work-package.ts PipelineSchema.duration_ms at line 81: z.number().int().nonnegative().optional() is the correct Zod chain. The .int() validator rejects fractional values, .nonnegative() rejects negative values, and .optional() preserves the optional semantics for in-progress pipelines. No existing tests broke (1518 passing), confirming the MCP server never writes non-integer or negative duration_ms values.
All 4 acceptance criteria verified as met. Both changes are minimal, targeted, and fully consistent with surrounding code patterns.

comments.note: mcp-server/gui/public/styles.css: .wp-timing uses margin-top (spacing above) while .pipeline-meta uses margin-bottom (spacing below the element). This is a natural difference given their position in the rendered view — not an inconsistency. Both are correct for their respective contexts.

mcp-server/src/schema/work-package.ts: The Developer correctly noted that existing fractional duration_ms data (e.g. 5000.5) would now fail Zod parsing. Given the MCP server always writes Math.round() or integer milliseconds, this risk is theoretical only. If foreign data sources ever feed this schema, a data migration note in the changelog would be prudent.
No issues found. Both changes are correct, consistent, and minimal.

notes: WP-004: two cosmetic/schema fixes. .wp-timing now has styles matching the existing metadata block patterns. PipelineSchema.duration_ms is now strictly typed as non-negative integer. 1518/1518 Vitest tests pass.

All 4 AC confirmed met. CSS token and Zod schema changes are consistent with existing patterns. Documentation agent may wish to note the stricter duration_ms typing in the schema changelog or API reference.
